apis.name: Jooble REST API
apis.saudi: Likely: Jooble runs sa.jooble.org (its pages appeared in search results), and the docs say each country domain has its own key. Not tested without a key.
apis.freeLimit: Free plan: 100 requests per day per key (one country), resets at midnight UTC; more on request through support.
apis.key: Fill in the form on jooble.org/api/about (name, position, email, website, phone). One key per country: request it for sa.jooble.org.
apis.displayTerms: API page: you may post the results on your website in your own design. Terms of Service not read in full. Each result has link, source, company, location, snippet, updated.

apis.name: Careerjet API
apis.saudi: Unconfirmed: locale_code takes the form language_COUNTRY, but the docs page does not list the supported codes, so en_SA is not confirmed (an unsupported code returns HTTP 400).
apis.freeLimit: Not stated on the docs page.
apis.key: API key from a Careerjet Publisher account (publisher registration); sent as basic-auth user name with an empty password.
apis.displayTerms: Not stated on the docs page. Every call must include the end user's IP and user agent (403 without them), so calls go through our server on the user's behalf.

apis.name: JSearch (OpenWeb Ninja / RapidAPI)
apis.saudi: Unconfirmed: the OpenWeb Ninja page does not list countries. The RapidAPI pages load only with JavaScript, so their parameters and plans could not be read.
apis.freeLimit: Not confirmed. The figure of about 200 free requests a month could not be checked on any page that opens without sign-up.
apis.key: Sign up on the OpenWeb Ninja developer portal (app.openwebninja.com) or subscribe on RapidAPI.
apis.displayTerms: Not stated on the page opened. Its page says it returns postings 'from LinkedIn, Indeed, Glassdoor, ZipRecruiter, and all public job sites via Google for Jobs'.

apiRecommendation.name: Jooble REST API
apiRecommendation.why: It is the only one of the three whose public docs state a free limit (100 requests a day per key, reset at midnight UTC) and a simple request (POST JSON with keywords and location). It has a Saudi site (sa.jooble.org) and each country gets its own key, so ask for the Saudi key. Each result carries the original link, source, company and update date, which fits our cards. Its API page says results may be shown on your site in your own design. Careerjet's docs do not confirm en_SA and need the user's IP and browser on every call. JSearch's free quota and Saudi coverage could not be confirmed from pages that open without sign-up, and it resurfaces LinkedIn, Indeed and Glassdoor postings, the sites we chose not to scrape.
